title: implement raytrace_mesh

atoms.evidence: ray (O, D); s along D gives the distance after Dx scaling
same -D, B-A, C-A stack and inside-test as 0_1_5, now over (NR, NT, 3, 3)
einops.repeat(triangles, 'NT pts dims -> pts NR NT dims', NR=NR) AND einops.repeat(rays, 'NR pts dims -> pts NR NT dims', NT=NT) — double-broadcast for full (NR, NT) batch
mat = t.stack([-D, B - A, C - A], dim=-1) on (NR, NT, 3, 3)
A, B, C = triangles and O, D = rays after the repeat (first-axis unpacking); s, u, v = sol.unbind(-1)
dets = t.linalg.det(mat); is_singular = dets.abs() < 1e-8; mat[is_singular] = t.eye(3); ~is_singular in final AND
t.linalg.solve over (NR, NT, 3, 3) — two batch dims; markdown explicitly reminds 'most batched operations can accept multiple dimensions as being batch dims'
s[~intersects] = float('inf') — overwrites non-hits so subsequent min reduction skips them naturally
einops.reduce(s, 'NR NT -> NR', 'min') — explicit min reduction over the triangle axis

notes: 10 atoms — densest pure-geometry exercise. Generalizes raytrace_triangle from 1 triangle to NT triangles by adding a second batch dim throughout. New atoms vs 0_1_5: inf-masking (distance-vs-hit unification trick) and einops-reduce-min. The (NR, NT) double broadcast via einops.repeat is the load-bearing structural insight. Note s *= D[..., 0] is a one-off scaling step — no new atom warranted.
